title: How can eighteen horses still show five on each side?
description: The thief steals a second horse. The video finds how many corner horses the caretaker needs for eighteen horses, and how many more the thief can take.
teaching_notes: One idea: real horses equal the counted total take away the corner horses, and there are only four corners. Watch for children who think five on each side needs all the horses.

source: There are 18 horses. How many corner horses are needed so th
video_script.why: The child knows a corner horse is counted twice but has not yet linked the number of corner horses to the number of real horses.
video_script.substitution: Take the real number of horses away from the counted total to find the corner horses, then use all four corners to find the fewest horses.
video_script.anchor: Joseph reading the next page of the king's horse story, with the square stable drawn from above
video_script.wrong_answer: eighteen horses cannot show five on each side
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu thinks five horses on every side needs all twenty horses, so fewer horses cannot work.

final_answer.value: 2 corner horses are needed, and the thief can steal 2 more horses
final_answer.spoken: two corner horses are needed, and the thief can steal two more horses

maths_rules: 5 on each of 4 sides: counted total is 20
each corner horse is counted twice, so real horses = 20 - corner horses
a stable has 4 corners, so at most 4 corner horses; fewest horses = 20 - 4 = 16
the thief can steal 18 - 16 = 2 more horses
slip: five on each side needs all 20 horses, which is false
your turn: 9 on each side, counted total 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36; 33 horses; 36 - 33 = 3 corner horses; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: real horses equal 20 take away the corner horses, and four corners is the most. Wrong idea: five on a side needs all twenty. The stable from above stays on the stage; the sums go on the working board.

<bookmark mark='five'/>The caretaker wants to show five horses along each side of the square stable again.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many corner horses does he need, and how many more horses can the thief steal?

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>The count is twenty and the real number is eighteen. Twenty take away eighteen is two.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Put horses at two corners, and every side still shows five. That means two corner horses are needed.
<bookmark mark='four'/>A stable has only four corners, so there can be at most four corner horses.

narration: <bookmark mark='all'/>With all four corners full, the stable holds twenty take away four, which is sixteen horses.
<bookmark mark='steal'/>Sixteen is the fewest horses that still show five on each side. Eighteen take away sixteen is two.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The caretaker needs two corner horses, and the thief can steal two more horses.
